sentences.text: 1 FILE OF IV ADDITIONAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND JMFC AT MYSURU OF WOMEN POLICE STATION, MYSURU FOR THE OFFENCS PUNISHABLE UNDER SECTION 498(A), 506 OF IPC.

THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The petitioner has challenged the prosecution initiated against her in C.C.No.168/2014 pending trial before the IV Additional Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Mysuru, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 506 read with Section 34 of IPC.
2.

entities.text: IV Additional Senior Civil Judge and JMFC,
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The case of the prosecution was that the respondent No.2 herein lodged a report with the respondent No.1 stating that she was given in marriage to accused No.1 from whom she had two children.
She alleged that the accused No.1 was having illicit relationship with the various women and when she protested, he used to assault her and abuse her.

She claimed that she lodged a complaint on 04.03.2007 before the Women Police Station, who registered Crime No.23/2007,
which was thereafter settled amicably.
She alleged that her father had paid Rs.2,00,000/- to the accused No.1 so that he could engage in some business and earn his livelihood.
She alleged that the accused No.1 continued to have illicit relationship with other women and was forcing her to go out of the matrimonial home.

She alleged that the accused No.1 was found in the company of accused No.2, who was running a cloth centre at Kumbarageri street, near Uma Theatre and on coming to know about the same, she confronted the accused Nos.1 and 2.

The accused No.2 chided her and asked her to control accused No.1.
3.
Based on such complaint, the respondent No.1 registered Crime No.94/2013 for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 506 and took up investigation.
The respondent No.1 recorded the statement of CW.2, the son of the complainant and other official witnesses.

After obtaining wound certificate in respect of the injuries suffered by the defacto complainant, a charge-sheet was filed for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 506 read with Section 34 of IPC.
The Trial Court took cognizance of the said offences and issued process.
4. Being aggrieved by the same, the present petition is filed by the accused No.2.

5. The learned counsel for the accused No.2 contends that the accused No.2 was not related to accused No.1 and therefore, an offence under Section 498A of IPC was not made out against the accused No.2.

He contended that there was no allegation for an offence under Section 506 of IPC against the accused No.2 and therefore, the Trial Court without applying its mind to the material on record blindly took cognizance of the offences against the accused No.2.

2 6.

entities.text: Pujeetha J Sharma vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned High Court Government Pleader for the State, on the other hand, submitted that CW.2, the son of the accused No.1 did mention in his statement under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. that the accused No.1 was having illicit relationship with the accused No.2 and that accused No.2 was responsible for the marital discord between his mother and his father.
He therefore, submits that the charge against the accused No.2 for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 506 of IPC was justified.

7. The learned counsel for the respondent No.2/complainant is absent and therefore, this Court did not have the benefit of his arguments.
8.
Be that as it may, the records reveal that the accused No.2 was not related to the accused No.1 or the complainant in any manner whatsoever.
The allegation is that the accused No.1 had an illicit relationship with the accused No.2.

Section 498A of IPC makes only the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman liable for an offence under Section 498A of IPC and not a kept mistress or a person with whom the husband has illicit relationship.

9. An offence of adultery under section 497 of IPC no longer exists on the statute book and therefore,
the Trial Court could not have even taken cognizance of an offence under section 497 of IPC in so far as the accused No.2 is concerned.

Even otherwise, there was no material collected by the prosecution to justify the charge-sheet against the accused No.2 for the offence under Sections 498A and 506 of IPC.
10.
In that view of the matter, this petition is allowed.

The impugned prosecution of the petitioner/accused No.2 in C.C.No.168/2014 pending trial on the file of the IV Additional Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Mysuru, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 506 read with Section 34 of IPC is quashed.
However, the prosecution against the other accused shall continue.
